name: Nick Ho Porsche

description: High-octane motorsport portfolio with WebGL 3D depth-map driver/car parallax, GSAP SplitText telemetry HUD, fluid Lenis scroll, and interactive circuit track telemetry.

course_modules.title: WebGL 2.5D Depth Map Parallax
course_modules.text: Initialize a Three.js / WebGL shader pipeline using grayscale displacement depth maps (depth-map-car.avif and depth-map-nick.avif) to create real-time cursor perspective tilt.
course_modules.voice_script: Welcome to the Nick Ho Porsche Carrera Cup masterclass. In step one, we construct the WebGL 2.5D depth-displacement shader that creates 3D depth from 2D motorsport assets.

quiz.question: How does a 2.5D depth-map fragment shader compute parallax perspective?
options: By sampling depth texture luminance (depth.r) to displace UV sampling coordinates based on mouse position
By rotating the camera in 360-degree orthographic space
By rendering 500,000 polygon vertices in a geometry shader
By downscaling the canvas resolution to 240p
quiz.explanation: Depth maps encode distance from the lens into pixel brightness (luminance); multiplying mouse delta by depth.r simulates realistic optical perspective shift.

course_modules.title: GSAP Telemetry HUD & SplitText
course_modules.text: Implement the high-precision racing telemetry HUD with GSAP SplitText, animating RPM meters, lap time counters, and race statistics on scroll.
course_modules.voice_script: In step two, we engineer the telemetry HUD overlay. Using GSAP and SplitText, each character and digital metric animates with precision as the user navigates.

quiz.question: Why is SplitText effective for racing telemetry typography?
options: It splits DOM text into separate character spans allowing precise per-digit stagger and roll animations
It converts text into JPEG images
It translates text into German automatically
quiz.explanation: SplitText wraps characters or words into individual elements, unlocking micro-staggered flip, roll, and elevation effects ideal for digital dashboards.

course_modules.title: Lenis Smooth Scroll & Circuit Timeline
course_modules.text: Configure Lenis inertia smooth scrolling synchronized with ScrollTrigger for sticky circuit track breakdowns and career milestones.
course_modules.voice_script: Now, we synchronize Lenis smooth inertia scrolling with GSAP ScrollTrigger to achieve that signature 60 frames-per-second track navigation experience.

quiz.question: What role does gsap.ticker.add((time) => lenis.raf(time * 1000)) play?
options: It synchronizes the smooth scroll render loop with GSAP's internal ticker for zero jitter and exact frame alignment
It resets window scroll to zero every frame
It converts CSS animations to SVG
It limits the monitor refresh rate to 30Hz
quiz.explanation: Binding Lenis's RequestAnimationFrame loop directly to the GSAP Ticker guarantees that ScrollTrigger coordinates update in lockstep with smooth scrolling.

course_modules.title: Radial Sliders & Career Milestones
course_modules.text: Build the interactive radial track slider and driver career timeline with touch-draggable circular navigation and SVG circuit maps.
course_modules.voice_script: Step four brings the career progression to life. We construct the interactive radial track slider, allowing fans to inspect lap sectors and podium finishes.

quiz.question: What is the key benefit of radial dial navigation in interactive portfolio websites?
options: It provides a tactile, analog steering-wheel-like interaction that deeply reinforces the motorsport brand identity
It consumes less RAM than text buttons
It prevents mobile screens from rotating
It removes all CSS from the stylesheet
quiz.explanation: Motorsport UI benefits immensely from steering-wheel inspired radial inputs, creating a memorable tactile sensation for site visitors.

course_modules.voice_script: Finally, we apply the finishing aesthetic touches: the infinite marquee sponsor loop, Dutch orange laser accents, and WebP asset optimization.

quiz.question: Why is xPercent preferred over left/right pixel values for infinite marquees?
options: xPercent utilizes GPU-accelerated CSS transforms avoiding layout recalculation and repaint thrashing
xPercent works only in dark mode
quiz.explanation: Transform properties (translateX / xPercent) run on the browser compositor thread at 60-120fps without triggering expensive DOM reflows.

name: macOS Portfolio
title: macOS Sonoma & Sequoia Interactive Desktop
description: Authentic Apple desktop experience with physics-based magnification dock, draggable glassmorphic windows, live control center, spotlight search, terminal, and 70+ Big Sur icons.

course_modules.title: macOS Dock Physics & Magnification Curves
course_modules.text: Engineer the physics-based macOS dock where icon scales and translations dynamically curve based on Gaussian distance from the user cursor.
course_modules.voice_script: Welcome to the macOS Desktop architecture module. In step one, we construct the parabolic magnification dock using Gaussian distance formulas.

quiz.question: Which mathematical function produces the smoothest parabolic scaling for macOS dock icons?
options: Cosine squared decay based on normalized mouse distance
Linear subtraction with hard boundary clamping
quiz.explanation: Cosine squared falloff (Math.cos(distance/radius * PI/2)^2) yields smooth acceleration and deceleration without sharp inflection points.

course_modules.title: Window Manager & Draggable Panes
course_modules.text: Implement the desktop window stack manager with z-index elevation on focus, smooth window dragging with velocity dampening, and traffic light controls (close, minimize, maximize).
course_modules.voice_script: In step two, we engineer the window orchestration engine, handling coordinate transforms, active focus hierarchies, and macOS traffic lights.

quiz.question: How does the window manager ensure the clicked window always stays on top?
options: By maintaining an incremental z-index counter and setting it on the active window on mousedown
By deleting all background window DOM elements
By placing all windows inside separate HTML iframes
quiz.explanation: Incrementing a shared z-index counter on each focus event ensures the most recently interacted window floats above all others.

course_modules.title: Glassmorphism & Backdrop Filters
course_modules.text: Craft the frosted Apple glass aesthetic using backdrop-filter blur, specular edge highlight borders, and dynamic noise grain textures.
course_modules.voice_script: Step three focuses on visual design: the frosted glassmorphism menu bar, subtle translucent cards, and high-DPI retina border rings.

quiz.question: Why is saturate(180%) coupled with blur() in authentic Apple glassmorphism?
options: To compensate for luminance loss through heavy diffusion and keep underlying wallpaper colors vibrant
To invert colors on high-contrast monitors
quiz.explanation: Heavy gaussian blurring washes out color vibrancy; adding saturate(180%) restores the rich pop of the underlying wallpaper.

course_modules.title: Spotlight Search & Command Palette
course_modules.text: Construct the Cmd+Space global spotlight search bar with fuzzy app filtering, quick calculator evaluation, and keyboard navigation.
course_modules.voice_script: Step four integrates Spotlight Search. We build a reactive fuzzy-search engine that queries apps, files, and commands with keyboard shortcuts.

quiz.question: Which keyboard shortcut natively invokes Spotlight search on macOS?
quiz.explanation: Command + Space is the iconic macOS system shortcut for launching the global Spotlight search bar.

course_modules.title: Dynamic Wallpapers & Theme Sync
course_modules.text: Wire up the Control Center theme engine supporting Sonoma, Sequoia, and Ventura dynamic wallpapers with system dark/light mode synchronization.
course_modules.voice_script: Finally, in step five, we assemble the System Settings and Control Center, enabling real-time wallpaper shifts and brightness dimming.

quiz.question: What web storage mechanism allows the user's custom wallpaper choice to persist across browser sessions?
quiz.explanation: localStorage persists key-value data indefinitely across browser reloads without requiring server round-trips.
